briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Tax-Repeal Momentum Hits Michigan as Federal Courts Clear the Path for Rescheduling
briefs.top: Michigan operators are catching real political tailwind on the 24% wholesale tax — a gubernatorial candidate is campaigning on killing it and a new repeal bill just dropped in Lansing — while new stores keep opening in Ann Arbor and beyond. Nationally, a federal appeals court just upheld cannabis rescheduling, Compass Pathways landed a fast-track FDA voucher for its psilocybin drug, and Curaleaf's hostile Aurora bid shows real money still chasing consolidation.

local.text: New Standard debuts flagship Ann Arbor store — the retailer ran giveaways and discounts for its opening weekend as it staked a claim in one of the state's most competitive dispensary markets.

Muskegon's Fields Cannary eyes fall opening — the hospitality-forward project is building a retail cannabis dispensary paired with a full-service restaurant, pushing the format further than most Michigan shops have gone.
John James vows to repeal marijuana tax — the GOP governor nominee is proposing to "repeal or sharply reduce" the 24% wholesale tax and courting industry donors as he heads into the fall campaign.
Michigan Supreme Court limits weed-odor car searches — police can no longer search a vehicle on smell alone, a ruling that already helped one Kent County gun charge head toward dismissal.

Tax revenue misses target, new repeal bill filed — the wholesale tax brought in roughly $34-37 million per quarter against a $105 million projection, and a Republican lawmaker's House Bill 6224 now aims to scrap it outright.

national.text: Federal court upholds medical marijuana rescheduling — the D.C. Circuit rejected a challenge from reclassification opponents this week, keeping marijuana's move to Schedule III intact and clearing a legal cloud for medical operators.
DEA's own brief backs full Schedule III move — the agency told the court in its final post-hearing brief that cannabis no longer meets the statutory criteria to stay in Schedule I.

Compass Pathways lands FDA priority voucher — regulators granted a rolling NDA review and selected COMP360, its synthetic psilocybin treatment for hard-to-treat depression, for the Commissioner's National Priority Voucher program.
Hemp THC crackdown pushed back to December — the federal ban that was set for Nov. 12 got a reprieve to Dec. 11 under a bill President Trump signed, buying the industry more runway.

Curaleaf presses hostile $4-a-share Aurora bid — the MSO's takeover offer carries a 45% premium and would create a combined company with more than $1.5 billion in pro forma revenue, even as Aurora's board urges shareholders to reject it.
